title: Electricity today
summary: A short comic piece in the style of a children's science primer, presented as a lesson on electricity. It opens with a playful experiment about static shocks from scuffing across carpet, then offers a mock history of the field, casting Benjamin Franklin, Galvani, and Thomas Edison as "Electrical Pioneers" with absurd anecdotes: Franklin's kite flight leaves him speaking in proverbs, Galvani's twitching frog legs lead to a joke about veterinary frog repair, and Edison's supposed invention of the electric company is mocked as a scheme to resell the same electricity repeatedly. The text closes with a jab at modern lasers, which can vaporize a bulldozer or perform eye surgery depending on the power setting. The humour relies on deadpan misinformation, mock-earnest tone, and wordplay on scientific terminology. The author is not named in the excerpt, and the text appears to be a humorous or satirical essay rather than a serious textbook.
